::: {.cite-bar .domain-intelligence}
[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Pub. L. 108-458]{.cite} [118 Stat. 3638]{.cite} [50 U.S.C. 3023 et seq.]{.cite}
:::

Carried out the main recommendations of the 9/11 Commission. It separated leadership of the intelligence community from leadership of the CIA by creating the Director of National Intelligence.

## Key provisions

- Created the Director of National Intelligence with budget and tasking authority across the intelligence community.
- Established the National Counterterrorism Center.
- Created the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board.
- Sec. 6001: the lone wolf provision, allowing FISA surveillance of non-U.S. persons engaged in terrorism without a link to a foreign power.
- Mandated an information sharing environment and security clearance reform.

## Why it matters

The most significant restructuring of intelligence since the [National Security Act](nsa-1947.qmd), which it amends. How much real authority the Director has over agencies inside the Defense Department remains the standing question about it.

## Current status

In force. Its lone wolf amendment to FISA carried a sunset and lapsed in March 2020.
